slides.title: 5 winter heating myths that cost you money, or worse

slides.myth: Turning the heat down while you're out wastes energy, since it works harder to warm back up.
slides.fact: The Department of Energy calls that a misconception. Turning it back 7 to 10°F for 8 hours a day can save up to 10% a year on heating and cooling.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver

slides.myth: A power strip is fine for a space heater.
slides.fact: Plug it straight into a wall outlet. Space heaters pull a lot of power, and power strips and extension cords can overheat and start a fire.

slides.myth: It's OK to leave a space heater running while you sleep.
slides.fact: Turn it off when you leave the room or go to bed. Keep it at least 3 feet from bedding, curtains and anything else that can burn.

slides.myth: A fireplace helps heat the whole house.
slides.fact: A traditional open fireplace sends much of its heat up the chimney, and the draft can pull warm air out of the room too. Close the damper when there's no fire.
slides.source: U.S. EPA and DOE Energy Saver

slides.myth: Heat pumps stop working once it's freezing outside.
slides.fact: Cold-climate heat pumps are built to keep heating well below freezing. Older standard models lose more power in deep cold and may lean on backup heat.
slides.source: ENERGY STAR, NYSERDA Clean Heat, Mass. fact sheet
